# Tomato preprocessing reference fixtures

Generated by `training/create_mobile_preprocessing_fixtures.py` using Pillow.
The RGB files contain independently decoded, oriented, bilinearly resized and
center-cropped 224 x 224 reference pixels.

The rotated JPEG retains EXIF orientation 6, uses distinct horizontal/vertical
color gradients and 4:4:4 sampling. The lossless fixtures retain high-frequency
patterns for strict resize checks.
This controls for JPEG chroma upsampling and high-frequency inverse-DCT differences, so its comparison tests
orientation, resize/crop and NCHW normalization with the existing 5/255 maximum
pixel tolerance. The other fixtures are lossless PNG with a 1e-6 tolerance.

The previous high-frequency 4:2:0 JPEG mixed rotation validation with different
chroma upsampling behavior in Pillow and Dart. Pillow default versus fast JPEG
decoding alone produced up to 82 RGB levels of difference after resize/crop.
The production app still accepts normal subsampled JPEG photographs; this
controlled numerical test does not establish accuracy on every phone codec.
